basics.name: Julien Petit--Colboc
basics.headline: Computer Science Engineering Student – AI, VR & Robotics

items.description:
Main developer of Cerebro, an internal tool that matches consultant profiles to client requests for proposals (RFPs) using LLMs.

  • Built an AI pipeline that extracts, categorises and scores RFP × profile pairs, with reliable asynchronous batch processing; deployed in production after processing several hundred RFPs.

  • Calibrated the scoring prompt (temperature, required vs. desired skills, three sub-scores) and added short match justifications so users can check each score.

  • Started an annotated reference set to measure false positives and false negatives.

  • Built the daily report sent to about 10 sales staff; secured the API and web interface with authentication and SSO. Stack: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite, Docker, GitLab CI, Gemini.

Built a VR app for remote robot teleoperation (Scrum; C#, .NET, Unity, REST APIs).

  • Streamed a 360° camera mounted on the robot into an immersive VR view.

  • Secured robot access with AES-256 encryption.

  • Designed a real-time path interface to add, edit or delete waypoints.
• Conway's Game of Life in C++ (pair project, main contributor): MVC architecture, console and SFML graphical modes, toroidal grid, obstacle cells.

items.name: Blink
items.description: Python pipeline that generates short videos from a single topic: GPT-3.5 writes the script, Stable Diffusion XL creates the images, OpenAI TTS records the voice-over and Whisper generates the subtitles. Asynchronous API calls, automated editing with MoviePy.

items.name: Thrive
items.description: Cross-platform task manager (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Web) built with Flutter/Dart: local Isar database, categories, notifications.

items.name: Game of Life
items.description: CESI group project in C++. We built a Game of Life with a graphical interface: grid editable in real time, obstacles, adjustable speed, grid import and export.

items.name: Worldwide Weather Watcher
items.description: CESI group project on Arduino. A weather station with four modes, temperature and pressure sensors, an RTC clock, SD card logging and interrupt handling.

items.name: BB8
items.description: BB-8 robot of the CESI robotics club: a Raspberry Pi sends commands to an Arduino that drives the motors. I built the web control interface and its Python server.

items.name: UniLink
items.description: A university events platform, built as a team. Students browse a map of campus events and sign up; student unions organise them. React, Express, Prisma and PostgreSQL, containerised with Docker.

items.name: Photographer's website
items.description: A bilingual portfolio site for a photographer friend, which he updates on his own. Payload CMS, Next.js and Postgres, self-hosted with Coolify. Images are resized and converted to AVIF and WebP on upload.

items.name: AgentKanban
items.description: A local service that turns GitHub issues into tasks handed to coding agents (Codex), each in its own workspace. It follows OpenAI's Symphony specification.

items.name: The Arduino in pixels
items.description: A 3D model of an Arduino rendered live with three.js, then pixelated to five ink levels. You can rotate it with the mouse or a finger.

items.organization: BDE CESI Rouen – Head of Communication
items.description: Lead the student union's communication: Instagram content, event posters, photo and video coverage.
Built the remote control of a BB-8 replica: web joystick (HTML, JS) and a Flask server driving the Arduino over serial.

items.name: Running (half-marathon, March 2027), calisthenics, graphic design, travel

summary.title: Summary
summary.content: 4th-year Computer Science engineering student (work-study) at CESI, apprentice at CAPFI since January 2026. Main developer of Cerebro, an LLM-based matching system now in production, where I worked on making scores explainable and measurable. Previously a research intern at CESI LINEACT on VR teleoperation of robots. Seeking an internship abroad from June 2027 (12 to 17 weeks) in AI, VR or robotics, ideally within a research team.
